name: Iman
milestone_by_age_26: Discovered by American photographer Peter Beard in 1975 (age 20) while studying at the University of Nairobi; her first modeling assignment was for Vogue in 1976 (age 21), launching a career that made her one of the world's most iconic supermodels.
starting_point: Born in 1955 in Mogadishu, Somalia; daughter of a diplomat and a gynecologist; grew up in a prominent Somali family and later became a refugee before attending the University of Nairobi.
current_position: Retired supermodel, businesswoman, and philanthropist; founder of Iman Cosmetics; widow of David Bowie; net worth estimated at ~$100M; resides in New York.

trajectory.event: Discovered by American photographer Peter Beard while studying at the University of Nairobi; moved to New York to begin modeling.
Shot her first editorial spread for American Vogue, quickly becoming a muse for Yves Saint Laurent and other major designers.
Starred in the first Revlon campaign centered on Black women, the Polished Ambers collection.
Retired from full-time modeling after a 14-year career spanning five Vogue covers and campaigns for the world's top fashion houses.
Married musician David Bowie in a private ceremony; the couple became one of the most high-profile celebrity pairings of the era.
Founded Iman Cosmetics, a makeup and skincare line designed for women of color, filling a major gap in the beauty market.
Honored with the Fashion Icon Award by the CFDA in recognition of her decades-long influence on the fashion industry and advocacy for diversity.
Widowed when David Bowie passed away from liver cancer; became a vocal advocate for cancer research and grief awareness.

name: Vassily Ivanchuk
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1988 New York Open at age 19 (ahead of a field of grandmasters), was awarded the Grandmaster title in 1988, tied for first at the World Junior Chess Championship, and won the elite Linares super-tournament in 1989 at age 20.
starting_point: Born in 1969 in Kopychyntsi, Ukrainian SSR; father was a lawyer, mother a physics teacher; began playing chess at age 6 after receiving a magnetic chess set from his father.
current_position: Active Ukrainian chess grandmaster; FIDE rating ~2634 (2026); still competing professionally at age 57.

trajectory.event: Won the USSR Junior Chess Championship and earned bronze in the Ukrainian Chess Championship, marking his emergence as a top junior talent.
Won the European Junior Chess Championship in Groningen and earned the International Master title.
Won the 1988 New York Open ahead of a field of grandmasters, tied for first at the World Junior Championship, and was awarded the Grandmaster title by FIDE.
Won the elite Linares super-tournament, finishing half a point ahead of Karpov and a field of top-ten players.
Won Linares again, defeating world champion Garry Kasparov in their head-to-head game; reached world No. 2 ranking for the first time.
Reached the final of the FIDE World Championship but lost to compatriot Ruslan Ponomariov.
Won the World Blitz Championship and achieved a peak FIDE rating of 2787, reaching world No. 2 for the third time.
Won the World Rapid Championship, cementing his reputation as one of the most versatile and creative players in chess history.

name: Dikembe Mutombo
milestone_by_age_26: Selected 4th overall in the 1991 NBA draft at age 25 and named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team in 1992; was a 2x Big East Defensive Player of the Year and All-American at Georgetown by age 25.
starting_point: Born in 1966 in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo; one of ten children; grew up with aspirations of becoming a doctor; started playing basketball at age 16.
current_position: Died September 30, 2024 at age 58; final role: NBA global ambassador and humanitarian; retired in 2009 as second all-time in NBA career blocked shots (3,289).

trajectory.event: Moved to Washington, D.C. on an academic scholarship to attend Georgetown University, initially planning to study medicine before joining the basketball team under coach John Thompson.
Selected 4th overall by the Denver Nuggets in the 1991 NBA Draft after a dominant collegiate career as a 2x Big East Defensive Player of the Year.
Named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team after averaging 16.6 points, 12.3 rebounds, and 3.0 blocks per game in his debut season.
Led the NBA in blocked shots for five consecutive seasons with Denver before signing with the Atlanta Hawks as a free agent.
Won his record-tying 4th NBA Defensive Player of the Year award and reached the NBA Finals with the Philadelphia 76ers.
Retired after 18 NBA seasons with 3,289 career blocks, second most in NBA history; became a global ambassador for the sport.
Passed away on September 30, 2024, at age 58, remembered as one of the greatest defensive players in NBA history and a major humanitarian for his work in the Congo.

name: John Walker
milestone_by_age_26: Ran his first sub-four-minute mile in July 1973 (age 21), broke the world mile record with 3:49.4 in August 1975 (age 23) becoming the first man under 3:50, and won Olympic 1500m gold at the 1976 Montreal Games (age 24).
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Papakura, New Zealand; raised in Manurewa in a modest family; began formal athletics at Manurewa Normal School, coached by Arch Jelley using the Arthur Lydiard training method.
current_position: Retired middle-distance runner; former Auckland Councillor; knighted in 2009 as Sir John Walker; lives in New Zealand.

trajectory.event: Ran his first sub-four-minute mile in July 1973, marking his emergence as a world-class middle-distance runner.
Won silver in the 1500m and bronze in the 800m at the Christchurch Commonwealth Games, both in world-record-setting races.
Broke the world mile record with 3:49.4 in Gothenburg, Sweden, becoming the first man in history to run under 3:50 for the distance.
Won the 1500m gold medal at the Montreal Olympics, becoming the third New Zealander to win that prestigious event.
Became the first person in history to run 100 sub-four-minute miles, a milestone of extraordinary career longevity.
Competed in the 5000m at the Los Angeles Olympics, finishing 8th in the final, before gradually winding down his competitive career.
Knighted by Queen Elizabeth II as Sir John Walker for services to sport and the community.

name: Sócrates
milestone_by_age_26: Began playing professionally for Botafogo-SP in 1974 at age 20, was named revelation (newcomer) of the Campeonato Paulista that year, and was the tournament's top scorer in 1976 at age 22.
starting_point: Born in 1954 in Belem, Brazil; father was a civil servant who loved literature and named him after the Greek philosopher; grew up in Ribeirao Preto and joined Botafogo-SP's youth system at age 15 while studying medicine.
current_position: Died December 4, 2011 at age 57; final role: football commentator, columnist, and medical doctor; remembered as one of Brazil's greatest midfielders and a symbol of the Corinthians Democracy movement.

trajectory.event: Made his professional debut for Botafogo-SP and was named revelation of the Campeonato Paulista in his first season.
Became the top scorer of the Campeonato Paulista with 15 goals, including seven in a single match against Portuguesa Santista.
Joined Sport Club Corinthians Paulista after completing his medical degree, becoming the pillar of one of the most historic Corinthians teams.
Captained the Brazilian national team at the 1982 World Cup, leading the celebrated squad known for its beautiful, attacking football.
Named South American Footballer of the Year, recognizing his status as one of the continent's premier players.
Co-led the Corinthians Democracy player self-governance movement during Brazil's military dictatorship, a landmark in sports and politics.
Named by Pele to the FIFA 100 list of the world's greatest living footballers.
Passed away on December 4, 2011, in Sao Paulo, remembered as 'Doctor Socrates' - a footballing intellectual and cultural icon.

name: Aleksandr Karelin
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in Greco-Roman super-heavyweight wrestling at the 1988 Seoul Olympics at age 21, having become world junior champion in 1987 and earned a place on the Soviet national team.
starting_point: Born in 1967 in Novosibirsk, Siberia; weighed 5.5 kg at birth; father was a truck driver and former boxer; began wrestling at age 13 under coach Viktor Kuznetsov, who remained his coach throughout his career.
current_position: Russian politician; member of the State Duma since 1999; retired Greco-Roman wrestler widely considered the greatest of all time; lives in Russia.

trajectory.event: Started training in Greco-Roman wrestling under Viktor Kuznetsov in Novosibirsk, initially considering quitting before his coach renewed his enthusiasm.
Won the World Junior Championships and earned a place on the Soviet national team, establishing himself as a rising star in super-heavyweight wrestling.
Won Olympic gold in Greco-Roman super-heavyweight wrestling at the Seoul Olympics, beginning an unprecedented 13-year undefeated streak.
Defended his Olympic title at the Barcelona Games competing for the Unified Team, remaining undefeated between Seoul and Barcelona.
Won his third consecutive Olympic gold at Atlanta, becoming the first wrestler to win the same weight class three times, outscoring opponents 25-0.
Elected to the Russian State Duma, beginning a political career while still competing at the highest level.
Lost 1-0 to American Rulon Gardner in the Sydney Olympic final, ending his legendary 13-year undefeated streak and six-year run without conceding a point.
Received the Olympic Order from IOC President Juan Antonio Samaranch, capping a career with 887 wins and 2 losses at the senior level.

name: Guillermo Vilas
milestone_by_age_26: Won the year-end Masters Grand Prix title in 1974 at age 22, defeating Björn Borg and Ilie Năstase, and finished in the year-end top ten for the first time, establishing himself as a major contender.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Buenos Aires, Argentina; raised in the seaside resort of Mar del Plata; turned professional in 1968 at age 16 during the first year of the Open Era.
current_position: Retired Argentine tennis player; inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 1991; resides in Monaco; widely regarded as the greatest South American male tennis player.

trajectory.event: Turned professional in the first year of Open Era tennis, making his Grand Slam main draw debut at Wimbledon in 1970.
Won his first career ATP title in Buenos Aires, defeating Bjorn Borg when the Swede retired hurt during the final.
Won the year-end Masters Grand Prix title in Melbourne, defeating Ilie Nastase in five sets, and finished in the year-end top ten for the first time.
Reached his first Grand Slam final at the French Open, losing to Bjorn Borg; peaked at world No. 2 in the ATP rankings.
Won the French Open and US Open, captured 16 titles in the year, and was rated world No. 1 by World Tennis magazine; won 128 matches with only 15 losses.
Won the Australian Open for the first time, defeating John Marks in the final; repeated the feat in 1979.
Inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame, two years after his retirement, having won 62 singles titles and 4 Grand Slams.

name: Roberto Carlos
milestone_by_age_26: Called up for the Brazil national team in 1992 at age 19, won two consecutive Brazilian league titles with Palmeiras (1993 and 1994, ages 20-21), joined Inter Milan in 1995 (age 22) and Real Madrid in 1996 (age 23), becoming their first-choice left-back; by age 26 (1999) he was a World Cup runner-up (1998) and established as one of the world's best left-backs.
starting_point: Born in 1973 in Garca, Sao Paulo, Brazil; grew up in a working-class family; joined Uniao Sao Joao's youth system at age 15, initially as a forward before converting to left-back.
current_position: Retired Brazilian footballer; works as a football ambassador and commentator; net worth estimated at ~$160M; resides in Spain and Brazil.

trajectory.event: Made his senior professional debut with Uniao Sao Joao, beginning his journey as a professional footballer.
Called up for the Brazil national team for the first time, representing his country at the 1992 Olympics.
Won the first of two consecutive Brazilian league titles with Palmeiras, forming a formidable left wing with Rivaldo.
Signed with Inter Milan in a 4.5 million pound deal but was often played out of position by manager Roy Hodgson.
Joined Real Madrid under Fabio Capello, beginning an 11-season tenure that would define his career with 584 appearances and 71 goals.
Reached the World Cup final with Brazil (lost to France) and won the UEFA Champions League with Real Madrid.
Won the FIFA World Cup with Brazil and a third Champions League title with Real Madrid; was runner-up for the Ballon d'Or.
Left Real Madrid after 11 seasons, having won four La Liga titles and three Champions League trophies; joined Fenerbahce.
Retired from playing after a stint with Delhi Dynamos in the Indian Super League, capping a career with over 1,100 professional appearances.

name: Evonne Goolagong Cawley
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1971 French Open at age 19 on debut, followed by the 1971 Wimbledon title, and went on to win multiple Australian Open titles (1974, 1975, 1976, 1977) and reach World No. 1 by 1976, all before age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1951 in Barellan, New South Wales, Australia; third of eight children in a Wiradjuri Aboriginal family; father was a shearer and farm laborer; her first racquet was a piece of wood from a fruit packing box; talent-spotted by coach Vic Edwards at age 11.
current_position: Retired Australian tennis legend; awarded Officer of the Order of Australia (1982); runs tennis development programs for Indigenous youth; lives in Queensland.

trajectory.event: Moved to Sydney to live with coach Vic Edwards and his family, attending Willoughby Girls High School while training intensively.
Won the French Open on debut and followed with the Wimbledon title weeks later, becoming the first Indigenous Australian to win a Grand Slam.
Won the first of four consecutive Australian Open singles titles (1974-1977), establishing her dominance at her home Grand Slam.
Reached the World No. 1 ranking for the first time, capping a five-year rise from Grand Slam debut to the top of women's tennis.
Won her second Wimbledon title, becoming the first mother to win the championship since 1914 and only the second woman in history to do so.
Inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame, having won 7 Grand Slam singles titles and 68 career singles titles.
Served as captain of the Australian Fed Cup team from 2002 to 2004, continuing her contribution to Australian tennis.

name: Jody Scheckter
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first Formula One Grand Prix at the 1974 Swedish Grand Prix at age 24, becoming the first South African to win an F1 race, and was a championship contender that same year.
starting_point: Born in 1950 in East London, South Africa; father owned a Renault dealership where Jody worked as an engineering apprentice; won the South African Formula Ford series in 1970 and moved to Britain to pursue racing.
current_position: Retired South African racing driver and businessman; 1979 Formula One World Champion; runs an organic farm in Hampshire, England; remains the only African F1 World Champion.

trajectory.event: Won the South African Formula Ford series and the Driver To Europe scholarship, moving to the UK to pursue a Formula One career.
Made his F1 debut at the US Grand Prix at Watkins Glen with McLaren, having progressed rapidly through Formula Ford and Formula Three.
Won his first Formula One Grand Prix at the Swedish GP with Tyrrell, becoming the first South African to win an F1 race and finishing 3rd in the championship.
Won the Swedish Grand Prix in the revolutionary six-wheeled Tyrrell P34, remaining the only driver to win a Grand Prix on six wheels.
Finished runner-up to Niki Lauda in the championship driving for Walter Wolf Racing, winning three Grands Prix including Monaco.
Won the Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Ferrari, clinching the title at the Italian Grand Prix; remains the only African World Champion.
Retired from Formula One at the end of the 1980 season after Ferrari struggled with the 312T5, ending his career with 10 race wins.

name: Claudia Schiffer
milestone_by_age_26: Achieved breakthrough as the face of Guess campaigns in 1989 at age 19, became Chanel's new face in 1990 at 20, and signed a record $6 million/year Revlon contract in 1992 at 22, becoming the highest-paid model in history—all well before 26.
starting_point: Born in 1970 in Rheinberg, Germany; father was a lawyer; grew up as the oldest of four children in a middle-class family; originally aspired to become a lawyer and worked in her father's law firm.
current_position: Retired German supermodel, actress, and fashion designer; married to film director Matthew Vaughn; net worth estimated at ~$70M; resides in the UK.

trajectory.event: Scouted by Michel Levaton, CEO of Metropolitan Models, at a nightclub in Dusseldorf; signed with the agency and flew to Paris for a trial photo shoot.
Appeared on the cover of Elle magazine in Paris, marking her first major magazine cover and the start of her international modeling career.
Starred in the Guess campaigns shot by Ellen von Unwerth, becoming the face of the brand and drawing comparisons to Brigitte Bardot.
Became the new face of Chanel under Karl Lagerfeld, walking in his fashion shows and cementing her supermodel status.
Signed a record $6 million per year contract with Revlon, becoming the highest-paid model in history at the time.
Held the Guinness World Record for the model with the most magazine covers, having appeared on over 1,000 covers worldwide.
Married British film director Matthew Vaughn; the couple have three children together.
Launched her own cashmere fashion collection, transitioning from modeling to design and business.

name: Sudha Murty
milestone_by_age_26: Became the first female engineer hired at India's largest auto manufacturer, TATA Engineering and Locomotive Company (TELCO), in 1974 at age 23-24, after writing a postcard to the chairman challenging the 'men only' hiring policy.
starting_point: Born in 1950 in Shiggaon, Karnataka, India; daughter of a surgeon and a schoolteacher; raised in a middle-class family that valued education; was the only female engineering student in her college.
current_position: Indian educator, author, and philanthropist; founder-chairperson of Infosys Foundation; nominated Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) in 2024; awarded Padma Bhushan (2023); mother-in-law of former UK PM Rishi Sunak.

trajectory.event: Began studying Electrical and Electronics Engineering at B.V.B. College of Engineering, the only female student in her class.
Became the first female engineer hired at TATA Engineering and Locomotive Company after writing a postcard to chairman JRD Tata challenging the 'men only' hiring policy.
Supported husband N.R. Narayana Murthy in founding Infosys, contributing initial capital from her savings; the company would become India's IT giant.
Established the Infosys Foundation, a non-profit charitable organization focused on education, healthcare, and rural development in India.
Awarded the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian award, for her contributions to social work and philanthropy.
Awarded the Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian award, for her distinguished service of high order in social work.
Nominated as Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, for her contributions to social work and education.

name: Javier Sotomayor
milestone_by_age_26: Set world junior record at 2.33m at age 16 (May 1984) and first senior world record at 2.43m at age 20 (September 1988), becoming the first person to clear 8 feet in 1989.
starting_point: Born in 1967 in Limonar, Matanzas, Cuba; scouted by basketball coaches for his height but directed to high jump; was afraid of heights as a child; began high jumping at age 14 with coaching and psychological support.
current_position: Retired Cuban high jumper; current world record holder at 2.45m (set 1993); lives in Havana, Cuba; the only person ever to clear 8 feet.

trajectory.event: Set the world junior record of 2.33m in Havana at age 16, announcing his arrival on the world stage; missed the LA Olympics due to Cuba's boycott.
Won gold at the 1987 Pan American Games in Indianapolis, his first major international senior title.
Set his first senior world record of 2.43m in Salamanca, Spain; missed the Seoul Olympics due to Cuba's boycott.
Became the first person in history to clear 8 feet (2.44m), a barrier previously thought impossible; also won World Indoor Championship gold.
Won the Olympic gold medal in the high jump at the Barcelona Olympics, the pinnacle of his career.
Set the current world record of 2.45m (8 ft 1/4 in) in Salamanca, Spain, a record that still stands decades later.
Won his second World Outdoor Championship gold in Athens, adding to his 1993 title.
Won Olympic silver at Sydney after returning from a doping suspension, capping a controversial but legendary career.

name: Vlade Divac
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for Yugoslavia senior national team at the 1986 FIBA World Championship at age 18 and won gold at the 1987 FIBA Junior World Championship; was an established NBA player with the Lakers by age 24.
starting_point: Born in 1968 in Prijepolje, SR Serbia, Yugoslavia; began playing basketball at age 12 with Elan Prijepolje; moved to Sloga Kraljevo at 14 and Partizan Belgrade at 18, rising through the Yugoslav basketball system.
current_position: Retired Serbian basketball executive and former player; former VP of Basketball Operations and GM of the Sacramento Kings; inducted into Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame (2019) and FIBA Hall of Fame (2010).

trajectory.event: Debuted for the Yugoslav senior national team at the FIBA World Championship, winning bronze; also played for Partizan Belgrade's senior team.
Won gold at the FIBA Junior World Championship in Bormio, Italy, as part of the legendary Yugoslav junior generation.
Won the European Championship with Yugoslavia and was drafted 26th overall by the Los Angeles Lakers; named European Player of the Year.
Made his NBA debut with the Los Angeles Lakers, named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team; won FIBA World Championship gold with Yugoslavia.
Traded to the Charlotte Hornets after seven seasons with the Lakers, continuing his NBA career as a starting center.
Selected to the NBA All-Star Game as a member of the Sacramento Kings, the peak of his NBA career.
Inducted into the FIBA Hall of Fame in recognition of his international basketball career, including Olympic silver (1988, 1996) and World Championship golds (1990, 2002).
Inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame, cementing his legacy as one of the first European players to successfully transition to the NBA.

name: Patrick Swayze
milestone_by_age_26: Made Broadway debut in Goodtime Charley (1976) at age 24 and won the leading role of Danny Zuko in the Broadway production of Grease (1978) at age 25, which led to film and television offers.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Houston, Texas; mother was a choreographer and dance instructor who owned a dance studio; father was a mechanical engineer and former boxer; began training at his mother's dance studio as a toddler.
current_position: Died September 14, 2009 at age 57; final role: actor in the TV series The Beast (2009); passed away from pancreatic cancer.

trajectory.event: Moved to New York City to pursue a dance career, training at the Harkness and Joffrey Ballet companies before joining the Eliot Feld Ballet Company.
Made his Broadway debut in the musical Goodtime Charley, transitioning from dance to stage acting.
Won the leading role of Danny Zuko in the Broadway production of Grease, which led to numerous film and television offers.
Gained recognition for his role in Francis Ford Coppola's The Outsiders, part of a celebrated ensemble cast of young actors.
Starred in Dirty Dancing as Johnny Castle, a low-budget film that became a massive hit; received a Golden Globe nomination and sang 'She's Like the Wind' (US #3 hit).
Starred opposite Demi Moore in Ghost, which became a massive box office hit; received his second Golden Globe nomination.
Starred in Point Break and was named People magazine's Sexiest Man Alive, cementing his status as a Hollywood leading man.
Passed away on September 14, 2009, after a 20-month battle with pancreatic cancer, leaving behind a legacy as one of Hollywood's most beloved leading men.

name: Mario Botta
milestone_by_age_26: Designed his first building, a two-family house at Morbio Superiore, at age 16, and by age 26 had apprenticed with Carloni and Camenisch, studied at the Art College in Milan and Iuav in Venice, and worked with renowned architects Le Corbusier, Louis Kahn, and Carlo Scarpa.
starting_point: Born in 1943 in Mendrisio, Ticino, Switzerland; from a non-architect family; wanted to work with images from an early age; apprenticed at an architect's office in Lugano at age 15 before formal architectural education.
current_position: Swiss architect and professor emeritus; founder of the Academy of Architecture at Universita della Svizzera Italiana in Mendrisio; continues to practice from his studio in Mendrisio at age 83.

trajectory.event: Designed his first building, a two-family house at Morbio Superiore in Ticino, at age 16 while still an apprentice.
Enrolled at the Art College in Milan for his baccalaureate after completing a three-year draughtsman apprenticeship with Carloni and Camenisch in Lugano.
Began studying at the Universita Iuav di Venezia, where he met and worked with Carlo Scarpa, Le Corbusier, and Louis Kahn.
Received his professional degree from IUAV with a thesis supervised by Carlo Scarpa; his graduation film 'Images of Liberation' was released as a theatrical feature.
Started his own architectural practice in Lugano, initially concentrating on single-family houses in Ticino that established his stark, geometric style.
Completed the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, one of his most internationally recognized public buildings.
Co-founded the Academy of Architecture at the Universita della Svizzera Italiana in Mendrisio, one of Europe's most prestigious architecture schools.

name: Arvydas Sabonis
milestone_by_age_26: Won three consecutive Soviet Premier League championships with Žalgiris (1985-1987) and the 1986 FIBA Club World Cup, while also being a key member of the Soviet national team from 1982, all by age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Kaunas, Lithuanian SSR; began playing basketball at age 13; by 15 was a member of the Soviet national junior team; made his professional club debut with Zalgiris Kaunas in 1981 at age 17.
current_position: Retired Lithuanian basketball player and businessman; president of Zalgiris Kaunas; inducted into Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame (2011) and FIBA Hall of Fame (2010); 6x European Player of the Year.

trajectory.event: Made his professional club debut with Zalgiris Kaunas, one of the oldest basketball teams in Lithuania.
Named European Player of the Year for the first time, recognizing his dominance as the best player outside the NBA.
Won the first of three consecutive Soviet Premier League championships with Zalgiris Kaunas (1985-1987).
Won the FIBA Club World Cup with Zalgiris; was drafted by the Portland Trail Blazers (24th overall) but was not allowed to play in the US by Soviet authorities.
Won Olympic gold with the Soviet Union at the Seoul Olympics, cementing his status as the best center outside the NBA.
Finally made his NBA debut with the Portland Trail Blazers at age 30, nearly a decade after being drafted; played seven NBA seasons.
Returned to Zalgiris Kaunas for a final two-season stint before retiring in 2005 at age 41.
Inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame, recognized as one of the greatest passing centers and European players in basketball history.

name: Miguel Induráin
milestone_by_age_26: Turned professional in September 1984 at age 20, won his first professional race at the Tour de l'Avenir, became the youngest rider to lead the Vuelta a España in 1985, and won a stage of the Tour de France in 1989, all by age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Villava, Navarre, Spain; grew up in a farming family; discovered cycling through his father and uncle, both amateur riders; joined the Spanish amateur team CC Villaves as a teenager.
current_position: Retired Spanish road racing cyclist; 5x consecutive Tour de France winner (1991-1995); Olympic gold medalist (1996); lives in Navarra, Spain.

trajectory.event: Became the youngest winner of the Spanish amateur road championship, showcasing the talent that would define his career.
Turned professional in September 1984 for the Reynolds team; won his first professional race, a time trial at the Tour de l'Avenir, a week later.
Became the youngest rider to lead the Vuelta a Espana after finishing second in the opening prologue; also made his Tour de France debut.
Won his first stage of the Tour de France, signaling the beginning of his dominance in the world's greatest cycling race.
Won his first Tour de France, beginning an unprecedented run of five consecutive victories (1991-1995).
Won both the Giro d'Italia and the Tour de France in the same season, becoming one of seven riders to achieve the Giro-Tour double.
Set the Hour Record at 53.040 km in Bordeaux, demonstrating his extraordinary time-trialling ability and physical capacity (resting heart rate of 28 bpm).
Won Olympic time trial gold at the Atlanta Games before retiring in early 1997, ending a career with 5 Tour wins, 2 Giro wins, and an Olympic title.

name: Lars von Trier
milestone_by_age_26: At age 25, won two Best School Film awards at the Munich International Festival of Film Schools for 'Nocturne' and 'Last Detail,' and had his graduation film 'Images of Liberation' released as a theatrical feature.
starting_point: Born in 1956 in Kongens Lyngby, Denmark; grew up in an unconventional family; later learned his biological father was Fritz Michael Hartmann, his mother's former boss; studied film theory at the University of Copenhagen before attending the National Film School of Denmark.
current_position: Danish film director and screenwriter; co-founder of Zentropa production company and the Dogme 95 movement; continues to make films despite living with Parkinson's disease.

trajectory.event: Began his career as a child actor on the Danish television series Secret Summer, starting a filmmaking journey that would span five decades.
Won two Best School Film awards at the Munich International Festival of Film Schools for 'Nocturne' and 'Last Detail'; added the nobiliary particle 'von' to his name.
His graduation film 'Images of Liberation' (Befrielsesbilleder) was released as a theatrical feature, attracting critical attention as nothing comparable in Danish cinema since Dreyer.
Made his feature debut with 'The Element of Crime,' winning the Technical Grand Prize at Cannes; the film began his Europa trilogy.
Co-wrote the Dogme 95 manifesto with Thomas Vinterberg, a radical protest against superficial filmmaking that influenced world cinema.
Released 'Breaking the Waves,' which won the Grand Prix at Cannes and established him as a major international auteur.
Won the Palme d'Or at Cannes for 'Dancer in the Dark,' starring Bjork, cementing his status as one of cinema's most provocative directors.
Released 'Melancholia' to critical acclaim but was declared persona non grata at Cannes after controversial remarks about Nazis during the press conference.

name: Luis Enrique
milestone_by_age_26: Made his La Liga debut with Sporting Gijón in September 1989 at age 19, joined Real Madrid in 1991 at age 21, and earned his first cap for Spain in April 1991, establishing himself as a top-flight professional and international by his mid-20s.
starting_point: Born in 1970 in Gijon, Asturias, Spain; grew up in his hometown and joined Sporting Gijon's youth system at age 11; came through the ranks as a striker before converting to a versatile midfielder.
current_position: Spanish football manager and former player; head coach of Paris Saint-Germain (Ligue 1); won the treble with Barcelona in 2014-15; considered one of the top managers in world football.

trajectory.event: Made his La Liga debut with Sporting Gijon in September 1989, beginning his top-flight professional career.
Joined Real Madrid and earned his first cap for the Spain national team in April 1991, establishing himself as a top-flight professional and international.
Won Olympic gold with Spain at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, a landmark achievement for Spanish football.
Made the controversial move from Real Madrid to arch-rivals Barcelona on a free transfer, becoming a crowd hero and eventually club captain.
Retired from professional football after 8 seasons at Barcelona, having played 558 official games and scored 144 goals across his career.
Won the treble (La Liga, Copa del Rey, Champions League) in his first season as Barcelona head coach, becoming one of the most successful managers in the club's history.
Appointed head coach of Paris Saint-Germain, continuing his managerial career at one of Europe's biggest clubs.

name: Dražen Petrović
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Champions Cup (EuroLeague) with Cibona Zagreb in 1985 at age 20, scoring 36 points in the final against Real Madrid, and repeated as EuroLeague champion in 1986; named FIBA World Championship MVP in 1986 and Best Athlete of Yugoslavia in 1985.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Sibenik, Yugoslavia (now Croatia); joined BC Sibenka's senior team at age 15 in 1980; came from a basketball-loving family in a small coastal city.
current_position: Died June 7, 1993 at age 28 in a car accident in Germany; final role: New Jersey Nets shooting guard; inducted into Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame (2002).

trajectory.event: Became a member of BC Sibenka's senior team at 15, reaching the Radivoj Korac Cup finals in 1982 and 1983.
Signed for BC Cibona, where he would win two consecutive EuroLeague titles and establish himself as Europe's best player.
Won the EuroLeague with Cibona, scoring 36 points in the final against Real Madrid; named Best Athlete of Yugoslavia.
Repeated as EuroLeague champion with Cibona; named MVP of the FIBA World Championship where Yugoslavia won bronze.
Moved to Real Madrid, winning the Spanish Cup and Cup Winners' Cup in his single season there.
Joined the NBA with the Portland Trail Blazers, becoming the first Croat to play in the league.
Traded to the New Jersey Nets where he became a star, averaging 22.3 points per game in his final season (1992-93) on 51.8% shooting.
Killed in a car accident on June 7, 1993, in Germany at age 28; inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2002.

name: Carlos Sainz
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Spanish Rally Championship in 1987 at age 25 with a Ford Sierra RS Cosworth, and successfully defended the title in 1988 at age 26, while also making his first World Rally Championship appearances in 1987 with Ford.
starting_point: Born in 1962 in Madrid, Spain; played football and squash as a teenager, was Spanish squash champion at 16; got his first driving experience at 11 in his sister's SEAT 600; made his rallying debut in 1980 in a Renault 5 TS.
current_position: Retired Spanish rally driver; 2x World Rally Champion (1990, 1992); 3x Dakar Rally winner; father of F1 driver Carlos Sainz Jr.; received Princess of Asturias Sports Award (2020).

trajectory.event: Made his rallying debut alongside co-driver Juanjo Lacalle in a Renault 5 TS at the Rally Shalymar in Madrid.
Won the Spanish Rally Championship with a Ford Sierra RS Cosworth and made his first World Rally Championship appearances with Ford.
Successfully defended the Spanish Rally Championship title, establishing himself as Spain's top rally driver.
Won the World Rally Championship drivers' title with Toyota, becoming the first Spanish WRC champion (nicknamed 'El Matador').
Won his second World Rally Championship title with Toyota, cementing his status as one of rallying's all-time greats.
Retired from the World Rally Championship after 196 rallies, 26 wins, and 97 podiums across 19 seasons.
Won the Dakar Rally for the first time, adding cross-country rally success to his WRC legacy; won again in 2018 and 2020.

name: Salvatore Garau
milestone_by_age_26: Became the drummer of the Italian progressive rock group Stormy Six in 1977 at age 23-24, performing on the critically noted album 'L'Apprendista' (1977), which was well received in progressive rock circles and released on the L'Orchestra label.
starting_point: Born in 1953 in Santa Giusta, Sardinia, Italy; studied at the Accademia di Belle Arti di Firenze (Academy of Fine Arts of Florence), graduating in 1974 before pursuing music.
current_position: Italian contemporary visual artist; former drummer of Stormy Six; participated in the 50th Venice Biennale (2003); lives and works as a painter and sculptor.

trajectory.event: Completed his diploma at the Accademia di Belle Arti di Firenze, establishing his foundation in visual arts.
Became the drummer of the Italian progressive rock group Stormy Six, performing on the critically noted album 'L'Apprendista' released on the L'Orchestra label.
Performed on Stormy Six's album 'Macchina maccheronica,' which continued the band's avant-progressive and Rock in Opposition style.
The band disbanded in 1983, prompting Garau's transition from music to visual arts.
Had his first solo show at Studio Cannaviello in Milan, dedicating himself to figurative art and coming to the attention of critics Luciano Caramel and Enrico Crispolti.
Participated in the 50th Biennale di Venezia and showed work at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, marking his international art career.
Participated in the Stormy Six reunion, resulting in the album 'Benvenuti nel ghetto' in collaboration with Moni Ovadia.

name: Kim Kyong-il
milestone_by_age_26: Selected to North Korea's 23-man squad for the 2010 FIFA World Cup at age 22, and represented North Korea at the 2005 FIFA U-17 World Championship and 2007 FIFA U-20 World Cup.
starting_point: Born in 1988 in Pyongyang, North Korea; joined Rimyongsu Sports Club's youth system; developed through North Korea's state-organized sports development pipeline.
current_position: North Korean footballer playing as a midfielder for Rimyongsu Sports Group in the DPR Korea League; continued involvement with the national team setup.

trajectory.event: Represented North Korea at the 2005 FIFA U-17 World Championship in Peru, scoring two goals in four matches; also joined Rimyongsu Sports Club.
Played in three matches at the 2007 FIFA U-20 World Cup in Canada; made his senior national team debut on October 21, 2007, in a World Cup qualifier against Mongolia.
Competed in the qualifying tournament for the 2008 Summer Olympics with North Korea's under-23 team.
Selected to North Korea's 23-man squad for the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa, the country's first World Cup appearance since 1966; did not appear in tournament matches.
Continued representing North Korea in international competitions and qualifiers through the early 2010s.

name: Kim Myong-gil
milestone_by_age_26: Named to North Korea's 23-man squad for the 2010 FIFA World Cup at age 25, the country's first World Cup appearance since 1966, having represented the national team in World Cup qualifiers from 2005.
starting_point: Born in 1984 in Pyongyang, North Korea; developed through the state-organized sports system; played for April 25 Sports Club, a military-linked team in the DPR Korea Premier Football League.
current_position: North Korean footballer (goalkeeper); continued playing for the national team through 2015 World Cup qualifiers; last recorded international appearances in 2015.

trajectory.event: Began representing North Korea in 2006 World Cup qualifiers, appearing in multiple matches including against Bahrain, Iran, and Japan.
Played in the 2005 EAFF East Asian Cup, including a clean sheet against South Korea in a 0-0 draw.
Named to North Korea's 23-man squad for the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa, the country's first World Cup since 1966; was in the squad for all three group matches.
Represented North Korea at the 2011 AFC Asian Cup, appearing in two matches.
Made his last recorded international appearances in 2018 World Cup qualifiers, including a clean sheet against the Philippines.

name: Klaus Ebner
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Großer Österreichischer Jugendpreis (Austrian Youth Prize for Literature) in 1982 at age 18 for the novella 'Das Brandmal,' and again in 1988 for the novel 'Nils,' establishing early recognition as a literary talent.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Vienna, Austria; mother was a hairdresser, father a salesman in home entertainment electronics; attended secondary school in Vienna where his first writing attempts began at age 12 with a short theater play.
current_position: Austrian writer, essayist, poet, and translator; writes in German and Catalan; member of the Grazer Autorenversammlung and Associacio d'Escriptors en Llengua Catalana; lives in Vienna with his family.

trajectory.event: Wrote a short theater play at age 12, rehearsing it with school friends though it was never performed; began submitting prose and poems to youth literature competitions.
Won the Grosser Osterreichischer Jugendpreis for the novella 'Das Brandmal,' establishing early recognition as a literary talent.
Started translation studies for French and Italian at the University of Vienna, while also working for a literary circle and Viennese literature magazine.
Won the Austrian Youth Prize for Literature again, this time for the novel 'Nils,' reinforcing his reputation as a promising young writer.
Published his first book on computer software in a German publishing house, beginning a parallel career as an IT author that produced nine books by 2004.
Won the Wiener Werkstattpreis, a prestigious Vienna literary award, marking his return to serious literary writing after years focused on IT and translation.
Published the short novel 'Hominide,' a significant literary work that expanded his reputation as a prose writer.

name: Didier Pironi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Formula Renault Eurocup in 1974 at age 22, then won the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1978 at age 26 and made his Formula One debut the same year.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Villecresnes, Val-de-Marne, France; father ran a successful construction business; half-brother of racing driver Jose Dolhem; studied engineering before enrolling at the Winfield Racing School at Paul Ricard, earning a scholarship to Formula Renault.
current_position: Died August 23, 1987 at age 35 in an offshore powerboat racing accident near the Isle of Wight; final role: former F1 driver and 1978 Le Mans winner.

trajectory.event: Won the Volant Elf competition at the Winfield Racing School, earning financial backing to race in Formula Renault for 1973.
Won the European Formula Renault championship, winning seven races with his own team set up at Magny-Cours.
Finished third in the European Formula Two Championship and won the Monaco F3 support race, earning promotion to Formula One.
Won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with Renault Alpine A442B alongside Jean-Pierre Jaussaud; made his Formula One debut with Tyrrell at the Argentine Grand Prix.
Took his maiden F1 win at the Belgian Grand Prix with Ligier, finishing fifth in the championship with several podiums.
Was leading the 1982 championship with Ferrari when a devastating crash during practice for the German Grand Prix at Hockenheim shattered both legs, ending his F1 career.
Killed on August 23, 1987, in an offshore powerboat racing accident in the English Channel off the Isle of Wight.

name: Pak Sung-hyok
milestone_by_age_26: Selected for the North Korea 2010 FIFA World Cup squad at age 20, having debuted for the national team in 2009 at age 19.
starting_point: Born in 1990 in Pyongyang, North Korea; developed through the state sports system; plays as a centre back and defensive midfielder for Sobaeksu Sports Club in the DPR Korea League.
current_position: North Korean international footballer; plays for Sobaeksu Sports Club in the DPR Korea League; continued playing through at least 2025.

trajectory.event: Debuted for the North Korea national football team in 2009, appearing in East Asia Championship qualifiers and international friendlies.
Named to North Korea's 23-man squad for the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa, the country's first World Cup appearance since 1966.
Continued playing for Sobaeksu Sports Club in the DPR Korea League, maintaining his position as a regular defender.
Maintained a long career with Sobaeksu, appearing consistently in the DPR Korea League through the late 2010s and beyond.

name: Pak Chol-jin
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for the North Korea national football team in 2003 at age 18, played in multiple World Cup qualifying campaigns, and was selected for the 2010 FIFA World Cup squad at age 25.
starting_point: Born in 1985 in Pyongyang, North Korea; developed through the state sports system; plays as a defender for Amnokgang Sports Club, a military-linked club in the DPR Korea League.
current_position: North Korean international footballer; defender for Amnokgang Sports Club; earned 44 caps for North Korea; last recorded international appearances in 2010.

trajectory.event: Debuted for the North Korea national football team in 2003 at age 18, beginning a long international career.
Represented North Korea in 2006 World Cup qualifiers and the EAFF East Asian Cup, becoming a regular in the national team setup.
Was a key player in North Korea's successful 2010 World Cup qualifying campaign, appearing in 11 qualifying matches.
Selected for North Korea's 23-man World Cup squad and played all three group matches (against Brazil, Portugal, and Ivory Coast) in South Africa.
Made his last recorded international appearances in late 2010 friendlies, finishing with 44 caps for North Korea.

name: Ari Vatanen
milestone_by_age_26: Won the British Rally Championship in 1976 at age 24 driving a Ford Escort RS1800, and competed in the World Rally Championship from 1974.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Tuupovaara, Finland; grew up in rural eastern Finland; began rallying in 1970 at age 18; debuted in the World Rally Championship at the 1974 1000 Lakes Rally.
current_position: Retired Finnish rally driver and former politician; 1981 World Rally Champion; 4x Paris-Dakar Rally winner; served as MEP (1999-2009); lives in France and Finland.

trajectory.event: Began his rallying career in 1970, competing in local Finnish events before making his WRC debut at the 1974 1000 Lakes Rally.
Debuted in the World Rally Championship at the 1000 Lakes Rally; won the Nortti Rally in an Opel Ascona, beating Hannu Mikkola and gaining wider attention.
Won the British Rally Championship driving a Ford Escort RS1800, establishing himself as a top rally talent on the international stage.
Took his first World Rally Championship victory at the Acropolis Rally, driving a Ford Escort RS1800 privately.
Won the World Rally Championship drivers' title with the private Rothmans Rally Team, becoming Finland's second World Rally Champion.
Signed with Peugeot to drive the new 205 T16 in Group B; won three WRC events including the 1000 Lakes, Sanremo, and RAC Rally.
Won the FIA World Cup for Cross-Country Rallies, adding to his four Paris-Dakar Rally victories (1987, 1989, 1990, 1991).
Elected as a Member of the European Parliament for Finland, serving until 2009 (later representing France); transitioned from motorsport to politics.

name: Filippo Inzaghi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Capocannoniere (Serie A top scorer) with 24 goals for Atalanta in the 1996-97 season at age 23, and was named Serie A Young Footballer of the Year, before transferring to Juventus and winning the Scudetto.
starting_point: Born in 1973 in Piacenza, Italy; grew up in a footballing family with younger brother Simone; joined Piacenza's youth system at 12, with loan spells at AlbinoLeffe and Verona before breaking into the first team.
current_position: Italian football manager and former player; head coach of Serie B club Palermo; regarded as one of the greatest strikers of his generation; 2x Champions League winner and 2006 World Cup champion.

trajectory.event: Made his professional debut with Piacenza, though he was loaned to AlbinoLeffe (1992-93) and Verona (1993-94) to gain experience.
Made his Serie A debut with Parma, scoring 4 goals in 22 appearances in his first top-flight season.
Won the Capocannoniere (Serie A top scorer) with 24 goals for Atalanta and was named Serie A Young Footballer of the Year.
Transferred to Juventus and won the Serie A title in his first season, scoring 18 goals and forming a prolific partnership with Alessandro Del Piero.
Won the UEFA Champions League with AC Milan, having transferred from Juventus in 2001; became Milan's all-time top international goalscorer.
Won the FIFA World Cup with Italy in Germany, scoring 2 goals in the tournament.
Scored both goals in the Champions League final against Liverpool, winning his second European title with Milan.
Retired from playing after 11 seasons at Milan with 126 goals in 300 appearances; transitioned to coaching, eventually managing Milan and several other clubs.

name: Gerhard Berger
milestone_by_age_26: Made Formula One debut at the 1984 Austrian Grand Prix at age 24 driving for ATS, and secured a full-season F1 drive with Arrows in 1985, establishing himself as an F1 driver by age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1959 in Worgl, Tyrol, Austria; father owned a truck company where Gerhard worked as a driver; multiple race winner in European Formula Three before moving up to Formula One in 1984.
current_position: Retired Austrian racing driver and motorsport executive; 10x F1 Grand Prix winner; former BMW motorsport director; lives in Austria.

trajectory.event: Made his F1 debut at the 1984 Austrian Grand Prix driving for ATS, finishing 12th on his home debut and 6th at Monza in his second race.
Secured a full-season F1 drive with Arrows-BMW, scoring his first championship points with a 5th place in South Africa.
Switched to Benetton-BMW and won his first Grand Prix in Mexico, earning a three-year Ferrari contract on the strength of his performances.
Won the Japanese and Australian Grands Prix with Ferrari in his first season with the Scuderia, establishing himself as a top F1 driver.
Won the Italian Grand Prix at Monza, the only race not won by McLaren-Honda that season; finished 3rd in the championship.
Moved to McLaren to partner Ayrton Senna, winning races and contributing to McLaren's constructors' titles in 1990 and 1991; became one of Senna's closest friends.
Won the German Grand Prix at Hockenheim with Benetton - his 10th and final F1 victory - before retiring at the end of the 1997 season after 210 Grand Prix starts.

name: Mohammed Ben Sulayem
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first FIA Middle East Rally Championship title in 1986 at age 24, becoming the UAE's first motor-racing champion. By age 26 he had won two consecutive MERC titles (1986 and 1987).
starting_point: Born in 1961 in Dubai, Trucial States (now UAE); studied business at American University in Washington, D.C.; began his rally career in the 1980s, competing in the Middle East Rally Championship.
current_position: President of the Federation Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) since December 2021; re-elected for a second term in December 2025; 14x Middle East Rally Champion; lives in the UAE.

trajectory.event: Began competing in the FIA Middle East Rally Championship, driving for Toyota and Ford in the regional series.
Won his first FIA Middle East Rally Championship title with a Toyota Celica, becoming the UAE's first motor-racing champion.
Successfully defended his Middle East Rally Championship title, beginning a dominant run in the regional series.
Won his sixth consecutive Middle East Rally Championship title (1986-1991), establishing total dominance in the series.
Retired from competitive rally driving after winning 14 MERC titles and 61 international events, making him the most successful driver in championship history.
Became President of the Emirates Motorsports Organization (EMSO), the UAE's representative body in the FIA.
Elected as FIA Vice President for Sport and member of the World Motor Sport Council, the first Arab to hold such a position.
Elected as President of the FIA, succeeding Jean Todt; became the first non-European to hold the position, governing global motorsport including Formula One.

name: Rudi Völler
milestone_by_age_26: Became Bundesliga top scorer with 23 goals for Werder Bremen in the 1982-83 season at age 23, was named German Footballer of the Year in 1983, and earned his first cap for West Germany in 1982.
starting_point: Born in 1960 in Hanau, West Germany; began playing football at age 8 in his father's team; signed with Kickers Offenbach at 17, weighing only 65kg and nicknamed 'Beanpole'; moved to 1860 Munich in 1980.
current_position: German football executive and former player; director of the Germany national team; 1990 World Cup winner; 1993 Champions League winner; lives in Germany.

trajectory.event: Signed with Kickers Offenbach at 17, beginning his professional career in German football.
Earned his first cap for West Germany; was top scorer of the 2. Bundesliga with 37 goals for 1860 Munich, firing the club back to the top tier.
Became Bundesliga top scorer with 23 goals for Werder Bremen and was named German Footballer of the Year.
Moved to Serie A club AS Roma, where he won the Coppa Italia and was runner-up in the UEFA Cup.
Won the 1990 FIFA World Cup with West Germany, scoring 3 goals in the tournament including a crucial equalizer against France in the semi-final.
Won the UEFA Champions League with Olympique Marseille in the 1992-93 season, though the club was later stripped of its league title due to a match-fixing scandal.
Retired from playing after a final stint at Bayer Leverkusen; later became sporting director at Leverkusen and manager of the Germany national team (2000-2004).

name: Cha Bum-kun
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest player in the world to reach 100 international caps at age 24 in 1978, won Asian Games gold medal in 1978, and signed with Eintracht Frankfurt in the Bundesliga in July 1979 at age 26, later winning the UEFA Cup in 1980.
starting_point: Born in 1953 in Hwaseong, South Korea; grew up playing football at Kyoung-shin High School and Korea University; became the youngest-ever debutant for South Korea's senior team in 1972 at age 19.
current_position: South Korean football manager and former player; widely regarded as the greatest Asian footballer of all time; nicknamed 'Cha Boom' in Germany; lives in South Korea.

trajectory.event: Became the youngest-ever debutant for South Korea's senior national team while attending Korea University.
Became the youngest player in the world to reach 100 international caps; won Asian Games gold medal with South Korea.
Signed with Eintracht Frankfurt in the Bundesliga in July 1979, becoming one of the first Asian players in top-flight European football.
Won the UEFA Cup with Eintracht Frankfurt, a landmark achievement for Asian footballers in Europe.
Moved to Bayer Leverkusen, where he would spend six seasons and score 52 goals in 185 Bundesliga appearances.
Won his second UEFA Cup with Bayer Leverkusen, cementing his legacy as one of the most successful Asian players in European football history.
Retired from professional football after 10 seasons in the Bundesliga with 98 goals in 308 appearances; later became a successful manager in South Korea.

name: Bonnie Tyler
milestone_by_age_26: Her debut single 'Lost in France' reached #9 on the UK singles chart in 1976 at age 25, and her debut album 'The World Starts Tonight' was released in February 1977, both before her 26th birthday in June 1977.
starting_point: Born Gaynor Hopkins in 1951 in Skewen, Wales; grew up in a Neath council house with a love for music; entered a local talent competition at 17, placing second, which inspired her to pursue singing professionally.
current_position: Welsh singer known for distinctive husky voice; career spanned 50 years; awarded MBE (2022) for services to music; continues to perform.

trajectory.event: Entered a local talent competition by her aunt, placing second to an accordionist; the experience inspired her to pursue singing, forming bands Bobby Wayne & the Dixies and Imagination.
Spotted by talent scout Roger Bell singing in Swansea's Townsman Club; signed with RCA Records and adopted the stage name 'Bonnie Tyler'.
Released 'Lost in France' which reached #9 on the UK singles chart, becoming a million-seller and leading to her first Top of the Pops appearance.
Released debut album 'The World Starts Tonight' in February 1977; follow-up single 'It's a Heartache' became a worldwide smash, reaching #4 UK and #3 US.

Collaborated with producer Jim Steinman on 'Total Eclipse of the Heart,' which became her first and only UK #1 and reached #4 in the US; the album 'Faster Than the Speed of Night' debuted at #1 in the UK.
Released 'Holding Out for a Hero' from the Footloose soundtrack; received three Grammy nominations for Best Female Vocal.
Awarded an MBE in the Queen's Birthday Honours list for services to music, presented by Prince William.

name: Adrian Smith
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Iron Maiden in November 1980 at age 23 and recorded on 'The Number of the Beast' (1982), which reached #1 on the UK albums chart and became one of the most influential heavy metal albums of all time, all before turning 26 in February 1983.
starting_point: Born in 1957 in Hackney, London; father was a painter and decorator; grew up in Clapton; became interested in rock music at 15 after buying Deep Purple's Machine Head; was inspired to take up guitar by friend and future Iron Maiden bandmate Dave Murray.
current_position: English guitarist and singer; member of Iron Maiden (1980-1990, 1999-present); continues to tour and record with the band at age 68; also performs with side project Primal Rock Rebellion.

trajectory.event: Formed the band Stone Free with future Iron Maiden guitarist Dave Murray, beginning a lifelong musical friendship and partnership.
After leaving school, formed the band Urchin (originally Evil Ways), which he led until their demise in 1980, developing his songwriting and guitar skills.
Joined Iron Maiden in November 1980, replacing Dennis Stratton; his melodic guitar style complemented Dave Murray's playing perfectly.
Recorded on 'The Number of the Beast,' which reached #1 on the UK albums chart and became one of the most influential heavy metal albums of all time.
Recorded on 'Piece of Mind,' continuing Iron Maiden's run of critically and commercially successful albums through the 1980s.
Left Iron Maiden after the 'No Prayer for the Dying' album cycle to pursue solo projects, forming ASAP and later Psycho Motel.
Returned to Iron Maiden, rejoining the band alongside Bruce Dickinson and creating the current three-guitarist lineup that continues to this day.
Continues to tour and record with Iron Maiden, one of the most successful heavy metal bands in history, with over 100 million albums sold worldwide.

name: Eros Ramazzotti
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Sanremo Music Festival main competition in 1986 at age 22 with 'Adesso tu,' having already won the Newcomers' category in 1984 and released a debut album with multi-million-selling singles across Europe by 1985.
starting_point: Born in 1963 in Cinecitta Est, a suburb of Rome, Italy; father was a construction worker and aspiring singer; began playing guitar at age 7; failed the conservatory admission exam and worked as a bricklayer and bartender before pursuing music.
current_position: Italian pop and rock singer-songwriter; has sold over 80 million records in a 40-year career; continues to record and tour internationally; lives in Italy.

trajectory.event: Competed in the Castrocaro Music Festival with the song 'Rock 80' but was eliminated in the first round; signed his first record deal with DDD shortly after.
Won the Newcomers' category at the Sanremo Music Festival with 'Terra promessa,' launching his recording career and releasing his debut album 'Cuori agitati' in 1985.
Won the Sanremo Music Festival main competition with 'Adesso tu,' cementing his status as a major Italian pop star; released the album 'In certi momenti' which sold 3 million copies.
Released 'Tutte storie,' which became his first album to chart in the UK and sold 6 million copies worldwide, expanding his international profile.
Released 'Calma apparente,' featuring the hit single 'La cosa piu bella' (I Belong to You); the album sold over 4 million copies and solidified his pan-European stardom.
Released 'Noi,' which debuted at #1 on the Italian albums chart and marked his 25th year in the music industry.
Continued touring internationally with his 'Infinite Battito d'Ali' tour, maintaining his status as one of Italy's most successful musical exports with over 80 million records sold.

name: Pavel Nedvěd
milestone_by_age_26: Was a key player in Czech Republic's run to the Euro 1996 final at age 23-24, scoring against Italy, and transferred to Serie A club Lazio in 1996 after winning three league titles with Sparta Prague.
starting_point: Born in 1972 in Cheb, Czechoslovakia; father was a footballer who played for Skoda Cheb; began playing football at age 5; joined Skoda Cheb's youth system and later moved to Dukla Prague in 1990 at age 18.
current_position: Retired Czech footballer; former vice-chairman and board member of Juventus; 2003 Ballon d'Or winner; lives in the Czech Republic and Italy.

trajectory.event: Joined Dukla Prague in 1990, beginning his professional career in the Czechoslovak First League and making 65 appearances over two seasons.
Transferred to Sparta Prague, where he won three Czech league titles (1993-94, 1994-95, 1996-97) and established himself as one of the country's top midfielders.
Was a key player in Czech Republic's run to the Euro 1996 final, scoring against Italy; transferred to Serie A club Lazio after the tournament.
Won the Cup Winners' Cup and the UEFA Super Cup with Lazio, establishing himself as one of Serie A's premier midfielders.
Transferred to Juventus for 41.2 million euros as a replacement for Zinedine Zidane; won Serie A titles in his first two seasons (later revoked due to Calciopoli).
Won the Ballon d'Or as European Footballer of the Year, becoming only the second Czech player to receive the honor; reached the Champions League final with Juventus.
Retired from professional football after 8 seasons at Juventus with 327 appearances and 65 goals; later became vice-chairman of the club.

name: The Undertaker
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WWF Championship at Survivor Series on November 27, 1991 at age 26, defeating Hulk Hogan to become the youngest WWF Champion in history at that point.
starting_point: Born Mark William Calaway in 1965 in Houston, Texas; father was a construction worker; played basketball and football at Waltrip High School; earned a basketball scholarship to Texas Wesleyan University before dropping out to pursue professional wrestling.
current_position: Retired American professional wrestler; 7x world champion in WWF/WWE; widely regarded as the greatest professional wrestler of all time; final match at WrestleMania 36 in 2020; resides in Texas.

trajectory.event: Dropped out of Texas Wesleyan University to pursue professional wrestling; trained under Buzz Sawyer and Don Jardine, making his debut in 1987 under the ring name 'Texas Red'.
Signed with World Championship Wrestling (WCW) as 'Mean Mark Callous,' a replacement for the injured Sid Vicious in the Skyscrapers tag team.
Left WCW and signed with the World Wrestling Federation (WWF) in October 1990, debuting as 'Kane the Undertaker' at the Survivor Series pay-per-view.
Won the WWF Championship at Survivor Series on November 27, 1991, defeating Hulk Hogan to become the youngest WWF Champion in history at that point.
Began his legendary rivalry with Kane, his storyline half-brother, at the Bad Blood pay-per-view, launching one of the most enduring storylines in WWE history.
Won the World Heavyweight Championship at WrestleMania 23, extending his undefeated WrestleMania streak to 15-0; also won the Royal Rumble match that year.
His legendary 21-match WrestleMania undefeated streak was broken by Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 30, one of the most shocking moments in wrestling history.
Had his final match at WrestleMania 36 against AJ Styles in a Boneyard Match, officially retiring from in-ring competition after a 33-year career.
